newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EMU to start on time with nine members - Bank Baer.
newsitem.headline: EMU to start on time with nine members - Bank Baer.

text.p: Europe's single currency project will start punctually on January 1, 1999 with nine members, Switzerland's Bank Julius Baer forecast in an upbeat assessment of prospects for economic and monetary union (EMU).

"The third phase will begin as an 'expanded core union' comprising Germany, France, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Finland, Ireland and Sweden," it said in its basic scenario, which it assigned a 45 percent probability.
"Italy, Spain and Portugal will probably join a year later."

Denmark and Britian will also take part "after two to three years" despite their opt-out possibilities, and Greece "somewhat later", the bank said. New EU members from central Europe would join in a continuing process.

It gave a 25 percent probability to a scenario in which all EU members except Britian, Denmark and Greece would launch EMU on time, and a 10 percent weighting to the possibility that only core countries would start the project.
Baer saw a 15 percent chance that EMU could be postponed and a five percent chance it would be dropped altogether. It played down the possibility EMU could collapse after 1999.

It forecast the euro would be a stable currency thanks to the new European central bank's independence, the proposed stability pact among members, and a new grid to link the euro with currencies of countries yet to join.

"Given the fact that most currencies are now close to their competition-neutral rates against the mark, one should expect -- despite the view of many market observers -- only small exchange rate fluctuations until rates are fixed on January 1, 1999."
It recommended investors prepared to accept some risk to buy high-yielding bonds from southern European countries.
